scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Fireside Trance of the High Atlas

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originates from the Shilha people of southern Morocco, with some historians suggesting a potential origin in Telouet.
Due to the lack of written records, the exact historical timeline remains undocumented, though it is now found throughout the High Atlas and Souss regions.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Ahwash celebrates weddings, births, and harvests.
It serves as a communal and spiritual practice, allowing participants to connect with their spirituality and express the experiences of the individual and the tribe.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed by two large groups, typically men and women on opposite sides, who alternate their performances of song, dance, and poetry.
The practice is a collective ritual that utilizes choreographic structures to manage the interaction between participants.
on_screen: Formation: Two large groups, typically men and women on opposite sides.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is performed using the tara (a type of tambourine), the tbel (drum), and the naqus (a metal instrument played with two iron sticks).
Listen for the tara, tbel, naqus.
A rhythmic, percussive soundscape dominated by frame drums and the metallic strike of the naqus, accompanying alternating vocal poetry.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned
Listen later: Berbères du Maroc "Ahwach" — Éditions Musée de l'Homme-CNRS

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Performances occur in village settings, often in front of a saint's tomb during religious holidays known as moussem.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The dance has developed independently among different villages, leading to variations in performance details.
Related to the central Moroccan dance known as Ahidous.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: The dance is often performed at saint's tombs during religious holidays; some communities restrict it due to the belief that the performance involves the devil or carries spiritual power that may offend the saint.
